title: Pitches that include specific local currency figures or name the microfinance institution tend to experience slower funding speeds for both men and women.
Pitches from women that highlight how the loan will benefit their family or the wider community tend to accelerate funding speed.
Pitches from women that highlight family or community benefits fund faster, while pitches from men that mention family obligations or school fees fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who explicitly mention their intent to repay the loan may fund faster.
Female borrowers who state a business duration of more than three years may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who use descriptive characterizations like 'hardworking' or 'dedicated' may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who include specific institutional boilerplate (e.g., BRAC) may fund faster.
Pitches from women that specify particular inputs, such as certified seeds or fertilizers, are associated with slower funding speeds.
Pitches from women that emphasize funding for children's education or school fees are associated with slower funding speeds compared to professional goals.
Female borrowers who mention asset ownership, such as owning a home, may fund faster.
Female borrowers who list specific products or goals beyond family welfare fund faster.
Specifying the number of years a business has operated predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Pitches that provide concrete financial figures or specific inventory lists fund faster regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who list the specific ages of their children fund faster.
Female borrowers who use generic template language fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention specific business struggles or risks fund faster.
Female borrowers who identify as married in their pitch text fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention contributing to the community or social causes fund faster.
